Performers
George Gershwin (piano), Paul Whiteman Concert Orchestra (jazz band), Paul Whiteman (conductor) Documented

The Library of Congress credits Gershwin as pianist and Whiteman as leader. Farrington’s essay additionally identifies Ross Gorman’s clarinet and Henry Busse’s trumpet. No complete session personnel list is asserted.

[1] [4] [5] [6]
Work version
Gershwin’s 1924 acoustic recording with Paul Whiteman’s band, in Ferde Grofé’s original jazz-band orchestration; abridged for two sides of Victor 55225 Documented

The selected source supplies a single, already-joined MP3 of both parts. Contrapunctus has not joined separate 78 sides. It is the complete issued abridgement, not an uncut performance of the score. Schiff’s Table 1 distinguishes these recording cuts from the cuts in the solo-piano arrangement. The three listening sections group the introduction, the faster dances, and the broad melody with its piano continuation and finale; their starts are passage-level editorial estimates, without bar alignment or aural review. The source does not identify the score or parts used at the session.

Recorded
1924-06-10 Documented

Recording date of both Victor sides; separate from the September release and the modern upload.

[4] [5] [6] [8]
Place
New York, United States Documented

City is documented. A particular Victor studio address or room has not been established.

[4] [5] [6]
Label
Victor, blue label Documented

Original commercial issue. The image accompanying the selected transfer shows the blue Victor label, but its relationship to the physical copy digitised is unknown.

[3] [8] [6]
Catalogue
55225-A / 55225-B Documented

Two sides of one 12-inch disc. Bolig dates publication to 5 September 1924; the same day’s Chicago Tribune advertisement lists both parts under 55225, price $1.50, beneath the heading ‘Out today’.

[3] [4] [5] [6] [7]
Matrix, take, sides
Part 1: C-30174, take 1; Part 2: C-30173, take 2 Disputed: sources disagree

The side-specific Library of Congress catalogue records and Bolig’s discography agree on these matrix/take assignments, which are preferred here. Farrington’s essay reverses the issued take numbers in its final paragraph. The selected upload supplies no runout photographs or transfer log, so its particular pressing and stampers remain unidentified.

  • Part 1: C-30174, take 1; Part 2: C-30173, take 2
  • Part 1: take 2; Part 2: take 1

Transfer
Unknown Unknown

Internet Archive identifies an uploader but gives no disc-transfer or restoration credit. The uploaded filename resembles a video title; that alone does not establish a transfer engineer or source chain before this upload.

[1] [2]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item was added on 18 March 2024. This is an upload date, not an established digitisation or restoration date.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

The archive lists the single MP3 as an original upload, with format ‘VBR MP3’. Playback equipment, stylus, speed, equalisation, noise reduction, pitch correction, and the method used to join the two sides are undocumented. No additional audio editing was performed for the Hall.

[2]
Composition rights
Public domain in the United States: Gershwin’s 1924 composition and Grofé’s original 1924 jazz-band setting Documented

IMSLP identifies first publication of the two-piano score in 1924 and explicitly distinguishes the US-public-domain 1924 jazz-band setting from the later 1942 symphonic orchestration. This assessment is confined to the original version heard here. Grofé’s orchestrations remain protected in many other countries; no worldwide clearance or permission for modern editions is asserted.

[10] [11]
Recording rights
Territorial United States public domain from 1 January 2025, on the documented published-1924 basis Inferred, not documented

Victor 55225 was commercially published on 5 September 1924. Under 17 USC 1401(a)(2)(A) and (B)(ii), the 95-year period plus five-year transition ended on 31 December 2024. The archive supplies no Creative Commons licence. This is a statutory US term assessment of the historical recording, not a worldwide licence; no independent creative restoration claim is documented in the upload.

George Gershwin, Rhapsody in Blue; George Gershwin, piano; Paul Whiteman Concert Orchestra, Paul Whiteman; orchestration by Ferde Grofé. Recorded New York, 10 June 1924; Victor 55225, issued 5 September 1924. Single joined transfer supplied by Internet Archive; transfer engineer unknown. Territorial US public-domain basis.
